question.text: A key LIMITATION of the clawback provision, as highlighted in Chapter 6, is:

answer.text: It applies only to Cat I, not Cat II
The clause is only as good as the GP's ability (and balance sheet) to refund excess carry previously taken
It is prohibited by SEBI for funds under INR 100 crore
It resets the hurdle rate to zero for future vintages

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6.3.2: 'this clause is only as good as the manager's ability to refund the excess return, so it is important that the manager has high credibility and a balance sheet to support'. An under-capitalised GP's clawback is a paper promise. The Trap: A is false (applies to both); C is false; D is nonsensical. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C stresses the same. In practice, robust LPAs require GP-level escrow (20-30%) + GP guarantees on clawback. Manager's Pro-Tip: As an LP, insist on a 'clawback escrow' built into every carry distribution (e.g., 25% held in trust for true-up at fund wind-up), plus GP personal undertaking. A GP resisting escrow is a governance red flag.
